details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh:217-255 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The incremental-scope conditional in the audit script is malformed, with the `elif`/`fi` structure broken around the `LAST_AUDITED_SHA == HEAD_SHA` path.
  WHY: Reviewers described both parse failure and incorrect control flow in this block; the highest reported severity is critical, and the broken nesting can prevent the script from running the intended change-gated path at all.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:192-192 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The outer `elif` guard separating `LAST_AUDITED_SHA` handling from the incremental-scope logic is missing.
  WHY: Without that guard, the scope resolver can fall through into incremental logic when only the SHA check should apply, which can produce incorrect scope decisions.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:306-327 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The final `gh issue edit` that persists `ai:security-audit-last-sha` has no retry/exit check.
  WHY: A transient API failure can drop the SHA update after the rest of the audit succeeds, leaving the marker stale and forcing the next run to do a full scan.
- scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh:103-112 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The `consumer_retro_enabled()` fallback uses raw `gh api ... --jq` when `_safe_gh_jq` is unavailable, which can leak error JSON into `var_value`.
  WHY: A non-2xx API response can be captured as non-empty text, causing the enabled/disabled check to evaluate incorrectly and mis-handle consumer retro execution.
- scripts/workflow_retro.py:671-675 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: `merged_pr_query_failed` is included in `has_activity`, but the flag must be reliably initialized and propagated across all payload-building paths.
  WHY: If failure paths do not set the flag before `build_weekly_retro_payload` computes `has_activity`, the fail-open logic can still misclassify activity.
- agents.md:187-193 and 568-575 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The consumer-facing clarifying guard and `workflow_retro_fanout.sh` entry are not mirrored in the consumer onboarding contract or `docs/INVENTORY.md`.
  WHY: New tracker issues in consumer repos can still trigger clarify runs and inventory lint can fail, which breaks the no-recursion-on-tracker-issues invariant shipped in this PR.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: When `repos_override` is empty, both scheduled and manual runs must load `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json` and then dedupe.
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml, the Resolve repositories step in the collect-logs job, roughly lines 89-120
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: `Line 90 still reads \`repos+=("${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}")\` inside \`if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "schedule" ]\` branch.` No diff hunk modifies this step, so scheduled runs still omit consumer repos.
- requirement: "adds change-gating so the scans only spend tokens when a repo actually changed" (and the detailed skip-if-unchanged + incremental scope contract described in the PR description and #3496)
  expected_change_site: scripts/security_audit.sh (the scope-resolution block around lines 217-255) and the Python post-filter
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The malformed `if`/`elif` nesting is still present, the `CHANGED_FILE_COUNT` regex guard is missing, the Python filter never receives the changed-files list on first/rewrite runs, and the SHA marker is written after the comment/follow-up steps.
- requirement: "Centralized consumer fan-out (WORKFLOW_RETRO_CONSUMER_FANOUT_ENABLED, default true)" with per-repo `WORKFLOW_RETRO_ENABLED` honoring and no-activity skip
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh:consumer_retro_enabled and the outer loop error handling
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The raw `gh api` fallback is still used, reopen/edit/label failures can be swallowed when called under `if ! run_consumer_retro …`, and the `has_activity` fail-open path in `workflow_retro.py` still interacts poorly with the fan-out skip logic.
- requirement: "The consumer-facing clarify recursion guard" (skip `ai:security-audit` / `ai:retro` in clarify.yml and the contract test)
  expected_change_site: tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py and docs/INVENTORY.md
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The consumer-repos onboarding contract and inventory entry are not updated to reflect the guard, and the contract test coverage for the clarify skip is absent from the delivered diff.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh:283-285 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The newly added `|| return 1` guards on `gh_retry gh issue reopen ...` and `gh_retry gh issue edit ...` ensure failures propagate through `run_consumer_retro`.
  WHY: Without those guards, bash can suppress `set -e` inside the `if ! run_consumer_retro ...` wrapper and silently report tracker-update failures as success.
Requirement: The judge-fix commit (708bdfe) explicitly committed to "1) `.github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml` around the `Resolve repositories` step (current lines 89-120): remove the schedule-only branch that does `repos+=("${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}")`. When `repos_override` is empty, both scheduled and manual runs must load `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json` ... and then dedupe." The review-blocked judge (entry[16]) independently identified this same defect as SEVERITY: BLOCKER: "the scheduled weekly retro path still collects only the source repo, so consumer retro fan-out runs against a report that omits consumer workflow runs."
Expected change site: `.github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml`, the `Resolve repositories` step in the `collect-logs` job, roughly lines 89-120. The fix must replace or modify the `if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "schedule" ]; then repos+=("${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}")` branch at line 90 so scheduled runs also load `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json` and append `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}` with dedup.
Evidence of absence: The current file at line 90 still reads `if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "schedule" ]; then repos+=("${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}")`. No diff hunk in the original PR patch, any subsequent autofix run, or the last-run diff modifies this branch. The last-run diff touches only `scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh` (4 lines) and `tests/test_workflow_retro_fanout.py` (65 lines). The companion contract-test assertion (judge-fix item 2) is also absent — `grep -n consumer_repos tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_failure_contract.py` returns empty. Every consumer retro produced by the fan-out step will see zero workflow runs and zero merged PRs in the report, incorrectly trigger `has_activity=false`, and skip with `WORKFLOW_RETRO_SKIP_V1` — silently breaking the shipped feature on its primary trigger (the weekly cron).
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh:107-112 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `_safe_gh_jq` is unavailable, the fallback uses raw `gh api ... --jq '.value'` and can leak error JSON into `var_value`.
  WHY: A non-2xx response from GitHub can be captured as non-empty text, so the enabled/disabled check can evaluate incorrectly and mis-handle consumer retro execution.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:231-237 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The nested `if`/`elif` structure inside the `LAST_AUDITED_SHA` block makes the incremental logic unreachable when `LAST_AUDITED_SHA == HEAD_SHA`.
  WHY: A user cannot select incremental scanning on an unchanged HEAD because the control flow falls through the skip-if-unchanged path instead.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:192-192 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: There is no `elif` guard separating the existence of a last-audited SHA from the incremental-scope logic that follows.
  WHY: Bash can fall through into the incremental branch when only the SHA check is intended, which can leak incorrect scope decisions.
- scripts/workflow_retro.py:671-675 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `merged_pr_query_failed` is included in `has_activity`, but the flag must be reliably initialized and propagated.
  WHY: If the failure path does not set the flag before `build_weekly_retro_payload` computes `has_activity`, the logic can still evaluate incorrectly.
- agents.md:187-193 and 568-575 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The added `ai-security-audit.yml` wrapper is registered, but the consumer-facing clarifying guard and `workflow_retro_fanout.sh` are not mirrored in the consumer onboarding contract or `docs/INVENTORY.md`.
  WHY: New consumer tracker issues can still trigger clarify runs and inventory lint can fail, breaking the no-recursion invariant.
Requirement: "adds change-gating so the scans only spend tokens when a repo actually changed" (and the detailed skip-if-unchanged + incremental scope contract described in the PR description and #3496)
Expected change site: scripts/security_audit.sh (the scope-resolution block around lines 231-237)
Evidence of absence: When LAST_AUDITED_SHA equals HEAD_SHA, the `SECURITY_AUDIT_INCREMENTAL` check is unreachable because it is placed inside the `if [ "${LAST_AUDITED_SHA}" = "${HEAD_SHA}" ]` branch but only reachable via an `elif`. Users who want incremental scanning even on unchanged HEAD cannot enable it.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
